title: Lessons from Drone Attack on Oil Facilities in Saudi Arabia
what_it_is: Lessons from Drone Attack on Oil Facilities in Saudi Arabia

sections.label: Lessons from Saudi drone attack
sections.summary: Asked what lessons Singapore can learn from the Saudi Arabia drone attack and what the Government is doing to prevent and counter a similar attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Defence what lessons can Singapore learn from the recent drone attack in Saudi Arabia and what is the Government doing to prevent and counter a similar potential attack in Singapore.

sections.label: Assets detect alleged Saudi drones
sections.summary: Current assets would have detected the alleged drones used in the Saudi oil facility attack; SPYDER replaced RAPIER and ASTER-30 will replace I-HAWK.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The assets we have in place now would have been able to detect the alleged drones used in the attack on oil facilities in Saudi Arabia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The SPYDER system has replaced the older RAPIER system, and the ASTER-30 missile system will replace the I-HAWK system.

sections.label: SAF monitors global drone threats
sections.summary: SAF will monitor threat developments and learn from global incidents to respond to potential drone attacks commensurate with threat level, sustainably and cost-effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: SAF will continue to monitor threat developments and learn from all incidents that occur globally to provide appropriate responses to the spectrum of potential drone attacks that are commensurate with the level of the threat and are sustainable and cost-effective.

sections.label: Confidence in detecting and neutralising
sections.summary: Low-flying drones avoid radar, but with different sensors and responses, Singapore is confident it would detect and neutralise the alleged Saudi attack components.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: They are low flying, they try to avoid radar detection, you can have counter-offensive measures which deal with that using a different array of sensors, as well as responses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I would say the short answer is that, if the alleged components or platforms as in the Saudi attack were used, we are quite confident that we would have detected it as well as been able to neutralise it.

sections.label: Drone software with restricted zones
sections.summary: Certain classes of drones from certain manufacturers have built-in software with coordinates of restricted zones so drones cannot fly in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For instance, certain class of drones that are by certain manufacturers have built-in software that you can key in, which incorporate coordinates of restricted zones so that the drones can never fly in.
